Ann Intern Med 2000; 132: 885–8. Granulomatous diseases. Although co-trimoxazole appears to be effective in reducing the incidence of bacterial infection in patients with chronic granulomatous disease,1-3 a disorder of leu- cocyte function associated with recurrent life-threatening infec- tion and granuloma formation, its use in systemic vasculitis is much more controversial. There have been a number of reports of benefit from co-trimoxazole in patients with Wegener’s gran- ulomatosis (p.1515),4-7 but even where benefit has been reported relapse appears to be common,6 and an analysis8 of the experi- ence of the USA National Institutes of Health in 158 patients, was sceptical of its value: only 1 of 9 patients given 960 mg twice daily by mouth had any prolonged improvement. Some evidence later emerged that addition of co-trimoxazole to maintenance regimens in patients already in remission reduces the incidence of relapse,9 although another study suggested that it might actually increase the risk of relapse.10 1.
